decisions.difference: A: (clinical_finding "Wound, non-healed" morphologic abnormality)  vs  B: (clinical_finding "Chronic wound" disorder), in tasks, priority rules and diagnosis rules
decisions.reason: The page says "non-healing wound", which "Wound, non-healed" names directly (and VHA's vocabulary already uses it); "Chronic wound" adds a duration the page does not state.

decisions.difference: A: (clinical_finding "Confined to chair")  vs  B: (clinical_finding "Dependence on wheelchair"), also in the pressure-ulcer rule and the three Q1 No negations
decisions.reason: The page says "in wheelchair"; "Dependence on wheelchair" names the wheelchair, "Confined to chair" does not.

decisions.difference: A: infection = Infected ulcer of skin or Local infection of wound  vs  B: also any one of Erythema, Warm skin, Swelling (also in check_for)
decisions.final_expr: (or (clinical_finding "Infected ulcer of skin") (clinical_finding "Local infection of wound"))
decisions.reason: The page's criterion is "Infection", with "(surrounding skin red/warm/swollen)" as its description; B's unsited single signs would make any swelling or redness count as infection, but the page does not say whether the signs alone suffice.

decisions.difference: A: Skin ulcer with finding_site at 8 pressure sites (occiput, spine, scapula, elbow, sacrum, hip, ankle, heel)  vs  B: none (site half not modelled)
decisions.reason: Q1 is an "and": "bedridden/in wheelchair and is ulcer in common pressure ulcer site (see below)"; A encodes both halves from the figure, B drops the second and over-fires.

decisions.difference: A: arterial, venous and diabetic rules require Q1 = No  vs  B: they do not
decisions.final_expr: (or (and (no bedridden) (no wheelchair)) (and (no ulcer at each pressure site)))
decisions.reason: The flowchart reaches "Is ulcer on the lower leg or foot?" only on the No branch of Q1, so the later diagnoses require it.

decisions.difference: A: (clinical_finding "Weak arterial pulse" (finding_site "Foot structure"))  vs  B: (clinical_finding "Abnormal foot pulse"), in check_for, arterial rule and negations
decisions.reason: The page says "reduced" foot pulses; a weak pulse at the foot is that, while "Abnormal foot pulse" also covers biphasic/monophasic pulses.

decisions.difference: A: (clinical_finding "Swelling of lower limb" (qualifier Chronic))  vs  B: (clinical_finding "Leg swelling symptom" (qualifier Chronic)), in check_for, venous rule and diabetic negation
decisions.reason: The page asks about "chronic swelling of the leg" as an observation; "Swelling of lower limb" matches the words, while B's narrower concept is a reported symptom but is the one VHA's vocabulary uses more often.

decisions.difference: A: no lower-leg/foot site forms of the wound  vs  B: Chronic wound with finding_site lower leg / foot (check_for and arterial, venous, diabetic rules)
decisions.reason: Follows the trigger decision (no "Chronic wound"); the page asks "Is ulcer on the lower leg or foot?", which "Skin ulcer" with those sites already covers.

decisions.difference: A: critical limb ischaemia rule without the ulcer/wound  vs  B: with (or Skin ulcer, wound) as context
decisions.reason: The red box applies to "the patient with a skin ulcer or non-healing wound", so this page's CLI rule is scoped to that patient (with A's wound concept).

decisions.difference: A: (diagnosis "Ischemic ulcer")  vs  B: (diagnosis "Ischemic ulcer of lower limb")
decisions.reason: The branch only covers "ulcer on the lower leg or foot", so the narrower concept (is-a "Ischemic ulcer") is exact.

decisions.difference: A: two urgent rules (infection; critical limb ischaemia)  vs  B: one urgent rule with an or of both
decisions.reason: Same logic either way; the page lists two separate bullets, and two named rules keep them distinct.

decisions.difference: A: two tasks (urgent conditions; cause)  vs  B: one task
decisions.reason: Same items either way; the page separates the red box from "Identify cause", and splitting matches that.

notes: Both builds passed. Base is A (pressure sites from the figure and Q1 No negations follow the flowchart; B over-fired). From B: Dependence on wheelchair, Ischemic ulcer of lower limb, and the ulcer/wound context on the CLI rule. Several diff lines collapse into each decision (the trigger and wheelchair concepts recur in many rules). A's known issues for (no X) of sited/qualified findings are kept.
